draft.editor_notice: The room sponsor edits the draft. Everyone can review the structure and drafting guidance.
draft.title_brief: Tell readers what the proposal is about in one concise phrase.
draft.why_brief: Explain why the proposal is needed: context, concerns, or principles.
draft.what_brief: Explain what should happen: a decision, request, recommendation, or action.
draft.guidance_tip: Hover or tap a highlighted clause label for a short explanation of how to use it.
draft.edit_instruction: Edit the proposal below. Other participants can review the saved version while you continue drafting.
draft.ai.placeholder: Explain what the draft should do. No UN format needed.
draft.ai.input_hint: Write your idea in normal paragraphs. The AI will convert it into draft sections.
draft.ai.generate_hint: Use AI to turn your plain paragraphs into draft sections. Review the result before saving.
draft.ai.manual_available: AI-assisted draft generation is currently disabled. You can continue drafting manually below.
draft.title_help: Give the proposal a short name that tells others what it is about. Example: Improving Transparency for AI-Generated Personas
draft.title_example: Example: Improving Transparency for AI-Generated Personas
draft.why: Explain why the proposal is needed: its background, concerns, or circumstances.
draft.what: Explain what you want to happen: an action, recommendation, request, or decision.
draft.preambular_example: Example: Recognizing the increasing use of AI-generated personas in online communication…
draft.operative_example: Example: Encourages platforms to clearly disclose AI-generated personas used in public communication…
draft.preambular_choice: You do not need to use every opening. Choose one or more that best explain the background or reasons for your proposal.
draft.operative_choice: You do not need to use every opening. Choose one or more depending on the kind of action you want the proposal to take.
draft.guidance_help: Hover or tap the highlighted guidance beside a clause if you need help.
draft.save_help: — saves your latest changes so other participants can read and co-sign them. You can continue editing after saving.
draft.submit_help: — submits the last saved version and assigns its L-number. Save your latest changes before submitting. After submission, the draft can no longer be edited and no new co-signers can join.
draft.save_hint: Save your draft progress without submitting it to the proposal floor.
draft.submit_hint: Submit this draft and assign it an L-number. After submission, editing and co-signing close.
draft.cosign.explanation: Co-signing supports bringing this draft forward. It is not your final vote on the proposal.
draft.cosign.closed: Co-signing is closed because this draft has been submitted.
draft.sponsor_hint: The main sponsor owns this room draft and can edit it before submission.
draft.cosign.member_hint: This member has co-signed the draft.
draft.title: Title
draft.cosign.remove_hint: Remove your support from this draft before it is submitted.
draft.cosign.add_hint: Add your support as a co-signer before this draft is submitted.
draft.guidance.recalling: Refer back to an earlier agreement, discussion, principle, or event that is relevant to this proposal.
draft.guidance.noting: Point out a relevant fact, observation, or situation without strongly judging it.
draft.guidance.welcoming: Acknowledge a positive development, effort, or action that has already taken place.
draft.guidance.expressing_regret: Show disappointment about an undesirable situation or something that has happened.
draft.guidance.expressing_deep_concern: Highlight a serious problem, risk, or harm that requires attention.
draft.guidance.emphasizing: Stress a principle or point that is especially important to the proposal.
draft.guidance.decides: State a concrete decision or action that the group or body itself will take.
draft.guidance.requests: Formally ask a particular person, organization, or body to take an action.
draft.guidance.calls_upon: Strongly urge an actor to take action. This is stronger than simply encouraging them.
draft.guidance.encourages: Recommend or support an action without making it sound compulsory.
draft.example.recalling: Example: previous discussions on transparency and digital trust…
draft.example.noting: Example: the growing use of AI-generated personas in online communication…
draft.example.welcoming: Example: recent efforts to improve disclosure of synthetic content…
draft.example.expressing_regret: Example: the lack of clear disclosure in some online campaigns…
draft.example.expressing_deep_concern: Example: the potential use of synthetic personas for manipulation…
draft.example.emphasizing: Example: the importance of transparency, accountability, and digital trust…
draft.example.decides: Example: to establish a common guideline for disclosure of AI-generated personas…
draft.example.requests: Example: platform operators to provide clearer disclosure mechanisms…
draft.example.calls_upon: Example: relevant organizations to adopt safeguards against deceptive synthetic personas…
draft.example.encourages: Example: researchers and platforms to share best practices on transparency…

amendment.intro: Use the builder to compose UN-style edits. Add multiple operations; the system will compile them before submission.
amendment.builder_hint: Use this builder to create ADD, REMOVE, or REPLACE operations.
amendment.ai.describe: Describe your amendment in plain language

amendment.ai.hint: Describe the amendment normally. The AI will convert it into formal ADD, REMOVE, or REPLACE operations.
amendment.ai.generate_hint: Ask the AI to draft amendment operations from your plain-language description. Review before submitting.
amendment.ai.disabled: AI-assisted amendment generation is currently disabled. You can still create amendment operations manually below.

amendment.preambular_help: Changes the background, reasoning, or concerns — why the proposal is needed.

amendment.remove_help: Delete an existing clause or piece of text.
amendment.replace_help: Replace existing wording with new wording.

amendment.add_operation_hint: Add another amendment operation, such as ADD, REMOVE, or REPLACE.

tutorial.dashboard.your_dashboard_text: This is your starting point in d¡alogüe. Events available to you appear here.
tutorial.dashboard.events_text: Your available event sessions are listed here. Each event card shows its timing, status, and stages.
tutorial.dashboard.open_an_event_text: Select an event card to enter its Event Menu and access agenda setting, deliberation, drafting, voting, and decisions.
tutorial.dashboard.event_status_text: This badge shows whether the event is upcoming, live, or ended.
tutorial.dashboard.upcoming_event_text: Before an event begins, this countdown shows how much time remains until its scheduled start.
tutorial.dashboard.live_event_text: While an event is running, this area shows the current stage, remaining time, and progress through that stage.
tutorial.dashboard.ended_event_text: When an event has finished, its card remains available so you can revisit its records and outcomes.
tutorial.dashboard.event_stages_text: These labels show the stages configured for the event.
tutorial.dashboard.department_of_records: Use the Department of Records to review material preserved from the deliberation process, including agendas, speaker records, and decisions.
tutorial.event_menu.event_menu_text: This is the main navigation hub for the event. Each card represents a stage or workspace in the deliberation process.
tutorial.event_menu.current_event_text: This shows the event you are currently participating in.
tutorial.event_menu.event_workflow_text: The cards below take you through agenda setting, deliberation, drafting, voting, and the final decision. Availability depends on the event schedule and your role.
tutorial.event_menu.propose_agenda_text: Submit an issue or topic that you want the event to consider. Proposed agenda items are reviewed before becoming part of the accepted agenda.
tutorial.event_menu.review_agenda_text: Authorized chairs or presidents review submitted agenda proposals and decide which items enter the accepted agenda.
tutorial.event_menu.view_agenda_text: See the agenda items that have been accepted for deliberation during the event.
tutorial.event_menu.general_floor_text: Join the broad discussion of accepted agenda items, take the floor, respond to other participants, and develop the direction of deliberation.
tutorial.event_menu.proposal_discussion_: Move from general discussion into focused drafting rooms, where participants can develop a formal proposal and gather co-signers.
tutorial.event_menu.view_tabled_drafts_t: Read draft resolutions that have been formally submitted, including their text, sponsors, co-signers, and proposed amendments.
tutorial.event_menu.proposal_floor_text: Discuss tabled drafts and amendments, participate in the speaker process, and vote when voting is opened.
tutorial.event_menu.decision_text: Review the recorded outcomes of draft resolutions and amendments, including voting results and final statuses.
tutorial.event_menu.open_and_locked_stag: Each card displays its current availability. A stage may be open or locked depending on the event schedule. Locked cards also explain when they open or why they are unavailable.
tutorial.propose_agenda.propose_an_agend: Use this form to suggest an issue for the event to consider. Your proposal will be reviewed before it becomes part of the agenda.
tutorial.propose_agenda.agenda_title_tex: Give the proposed issue a short, clear title so participants can immediately understand what it is about.
tutorial.propose_agenda.background_text: Explain the issue, provide enough context to understand it, and describe why it should be considered.
tutorial.propose_agenda.supporting_sourc: If useful, add a link to a report, article, official document, or other source that supports the proposal.
tutorial.propose_agenda.anonymous_submis: Choose this option if you want the agenda proposal to be submitted without publicly identifying you as the proposer.
tutorial.propose_agenda.submit_for_revie: When the proposal is ready, submit it for review. Submission does not automatically place it on the accepted agenda.
tutorial.propose_agenda.your_proposals_t: After submission, you can track your agenda proposals here and see whether each one is pending, accepted, or rejected.
tutorial.review_agenda.pending_agenda_pr: Agenda proposals waiting for a decision appear here. Review each proposal before deciding whether it should enter the event agenda.
tutorial.review_agenda.review_the_propos: Read the title, background, supporting source, submission time, and proposer information before making a decision.
tutorial.review_agenda.review_note_text: You may leave an optional note explaining or documenting the decision.
tutorial.review_agenda.accept_text: Accepting the proposal marks it as an accepted agenda item so it can proceed into the event's deliberation workflow.
tutorial.review_agenda.reject_text: Rejecting the proposal records it as rejected instead of adding it to the accepted agenda.
tutorial.review_agenda.recent_decisions_: Previously reviewed proposals appear here with their decision, time, and review note.
tutorial.review_agenda.reopen_a_decision: If a proposal needs to be reconsidered, reopen it to return it to the pending review queue.
tutorial.view_agenda.accepted_agenda_tex: This page shows the agenda proposals that have been accepted for this event.
tutorial.view_agenda.agenda_item_text: Each accepted item includes its title, background, proposer information, and submission time.
tutorial.view_agenda.supporting_source_t: When a source was provided, you can open it to review supporting material for the agenda item.
tutorial.view_agenda.accepted_status_tex: This badge confirms that the proposal passed agenda review and is now part of the accepted event agenda.
tutorial.general_floor_index.general_flo: The General Floor is organized by accepted agenda item. Choose the topic you want to enter and discuss.
tutorial.general_floor_index.current_eve: This shows which event these General Floor discussions belong to.
tutorial.general_floor_index.accepted_ag: Each card represents an accepted agenda item with its background information and proposer details.
tutorial.general_floor_index.agenda_item: Review the topic and background before entering its General Floor discussion.
tutorial.general_floor_index.agenda_info: This area shows when the agenda item was proposed, who proposed it, and any supporting source when available.
tutorial.general_floor_index.enter_the_g: Select the agenda title to enter its General Floor, where you can participate in the live deliberation.
tutorial.general_floor.current_agenda_te: This panel shows the agenda item currently being discussed.
tutorial.general_floor.discussion_text: Contributions from recognized speakers appear here as the discussion develops.
tutorial.general_floor.chair_controls_te: Use these controls to manage the current speaker and upcoming speaking order.
tutorial.general_floor.your_contribution: When you are recognized to speak, use this area to submit your contribution.
tutorial.general_floor.live_summary_text: This panel provides a running summary of the discussion as it develops.
tutorial.general_floor.speaker_queue_cha: Manage the speaking order here. You can recognize speakers and move the discussion forward.
tutorial.general_floor.speaker_queue_mem: See who is speaking, who is waiting, and request the floor from this area.
tutorial.proposal_discussion.proposal_di: Each accepted agenda item can have one or more discussion rooms where participants work together on possible draft proposals.
tutorial.proposal_discussion.choose_an_a: Each card represents an accepted agenda item. You can see how many discussion rooms already exist for it.
tutorial.proposal_discussion.view_existi: Open the room list to see existing discussions and choose one to participate in.
tutorial.proposal_discussion.create_a_di: You can also start a new room for this agenda item. Give the room a clear title and, optionally, a short description.
tutorial.proposal_discussion.start_the_r: Create the room when you are ready. The new room becomes a workspace for discussion, drafting, and co-signing.
tutorial.rooms_index.create_a_discussion: Start a new room for this agenda item by giving it a title and, optionally, a short description.
tutorial.rooms_index.existing_rooms_text: Existing discussion rooms for this agenda item appear here.
tutorial.rooms_index.room_text: Each room is a separate workspace where participants can discuss the agenda item and develop a draft proposal.
tutorial.rooms_index.room_sponsor_text: The sponsor is the participant who created the room and manages the draft being developed there.
tutorial.rooms_index.open_the_room_text: Open a room to join its discussion and view or contribute to the shared draft.
tutorial.room.room_discussion_text: Use this space to coordinate with the other participants working on this proposal.
tutorial.room.shared_draft_text: This panel contains the proposal being developed by the room.
tutorial.room.drafting_guide_text: This guide explains the basic structure: a clear title, preambular clauses, and operative clauses.
tutorial.room.co_sign_the_draft_text: Before submission, you can add or remove your co-signature to show support for this developing draft.
tutorial.room.sponsor_and_co_signers_tex: This area shows the proposal sponsor and the participants who currently support the draft as co-signers.
tutorial.room.editing_workspace_text: As the sponsor, you can edit and prepare the shared draft in this workspace.
tutorial.room.ai_drafting_text: You may describe what you want to draft here and generate a starting point to review and edit.
tutorial.room.manual_drafting_text: Write and revise the title, preambular clauses, and operative clauses directly here.
tutorial.room.save_your_work_text: Save your changes while the proposal is still being developed.
tutorial.room.submit_the_draft_text: When the draft is ready, the sponsor submits it for consideration as an official draft document.
tutorial.view_draft_index.tabled_draft_r: This page lists draft resolutions that have been formally submitted during the event.
tutorial.view_draft_index.active_drafts_: These drafts are currently active in the deliberation process. Select a draft to read its full text, sponsors, co-signers, and amendments.
tutorial.view_draft_index.open_a_draft_t: Each card shows the draft number, title, agenda item, sponsor, and submission time. Select the card to open the full draft.
tutorial.view_draft_index.reintroduced_d: This label means the draft was previously withdrawn and has since been returned to the active deliberation process.
tutorial.view_draft_index.withdrawn_draf: Drafts that have been withdrawn are kept here as part of the event record instead of disappearing completely.
A withdrawn draft is no longer active, but its identifying information and sponsor remain visible.
tutorial.view_draft_index.reintroduce_a_: Use this control to return a withdrawn draft to the active deliberation process.
tutorial.draft_detail.official_draft_tex: This is the submitted draft document. Its contents are now presented as an official draft rather than an editable workspace.
tutorial.draft_detail.co_signers_text: Support is recorded in two stages. Co-signatures made before submission appear as original co-signers, while later support is recorded separately in the addendum.
tutorial.draft_detail.late_co_signing_te: You can still add your support after submission. Your co-signature will be recorded in the document addendum rather than as an original co-signer.
tutorial.draft_detail.existing_amendment: Amendments that have already been proposed for this draft are listed here. Open one to read the proposed changes.
tutorial.draft_detail.propose_an_amendme: Use this area when you want to propose a specific change to the submitted draft.
tutorial.draft_detail.how_amendments_wor: An amendment can ADD new text, REMOVE existing text, or REPLACE existing text. Choose whether the change affects a preambular or operative clause.
tutorial.draft_detail.describe_the_chang: You may describe the amendment in plain language here. The AI amendment builder can turn your description into structured amendment operations.
tutorial.draft_detail.generate_operation: Generate a proposed set of amendment operations, then review them carefully before submitting.
tutorial.draft_detail.add_an_operation_t: You can build the amendment manually by adding one or more operations.
tutorial.draft_detail.amendment_operatio: Each operation specifies what to change, which clause it affects, and any text that should be added or used as a replacement.
tutorial.draft_detail.submit_the_amendme: Review all operations carefully, then submit the amendment. It will appear in the amendment list for further deliberation.
tutorial.amendment_detail.amendment_text: This page shows a submitted amendment to an existing draft document.
tutorial.amendment_detail.translation_te: Choose a language here to read the amendment in one of the supported translations.
tutorial.amendment_detail.original_draft: This shows which draft document the amendment belongs to. Select the draft title to return to the full document.
tutorial.amendment_detail.proposed_chang: This is the submitted amendment. Read the proposed changes here before the amendment proceeds through deliberation.
tutorial.proposal_floor_index.proposal_f: This page lists the draft resolutions currently being considered on the Proposal Floor, as well as floors that have already closed.
tutorial.proposal_floor_index.open_propo: These draft resolutions are still active on the Proposal Floor and can be opened for deliberation and voting.
tutorial.proposal_floor_index.draft_reso: Each card identifies the agenda item, draft number and title, sponsor, and any amendments associated with the draft.
tutorial.proposal_floor_index.sponsor_te: This shows the sponsor responsible for the submitted draft resolution.
tutorial.proposal_floor_index.open_the_d: Enter the draft's Proposal Floor to join its discussion and participate in voting when voting is available.
tutorial.proposal_floor_index.amendments: If amendments have been proposed, use this button to enter the Proposal Floor for an amendment.
tutorial.proposal_floor_index.closed_pro: Drafts whose Proposal Floor discussion has ended are listed separately here.
tutorial.proposal_floor_index.closed_dra: A closed floor remains visible as part of the event record, but it is no longer an active deliberation space.
tutorial.proposal_floor_index.closed_tex: This badge indicates that the Proposal Floor for this draft has been closed.
tutorial.proposal_floor.current_document: This panel shows the draft or amendment currently being discussed.
tutorial.proposal_floor.voting_text: Voting controls and results appear here when voting is opened.
tutorial.proposal_floor.discussion_text: The discussion record appears here as participants contribute to the floor.
tutorial.proposal_floor.speaker_queue_te: This area shows who is speaking and who is waiting for the floor.
tutorial.proposal_floor.speaking_text: When you have the floor, use this area to submit your contribution.
tutorial.decision.decision_text: This page summarizes the outcomes of draft resolutions and amendments considered during the event.
tutorial.decision.final_results_text: Use this page to review what happened to each submitted draft and amendment after deliberation and voting.
tutorial.decision.draft_resolutions_text: This section lists the submitted draft resolutions and their final or current outcomes.
tutorial.decision.draft_result_text: Each card identifies the draft, its sponsor and co-signers, its status, and the outcome reached during the event.
tutorial.decision.outcome_text: The outcome badge shows whether the draft was adopted, not adopted, withdrawn, reintroduced, or is still pending.
tutorial.decision.early_consensus_test_t: If an early consensus test was held, its YES, NO, and ABSTAIN counts appear here.
tutorial.decision.formal_vote_text: If the draft proceeded to formal voting, the final YES, NO, and ABSTAIN totals are shown here.
tutorial.decision.amendments_text: This section summarizes the outcomes of amendments proposed to draft resolutions.
tutorial.decision.amendment_result_text: Each amendment result identifies the amendment, the draft it belongs to, who submitted it, and its outcome.
tutorial.decision.amendment_outcome_text: This badge shows whether the amendment was adopted, adopted by consensus, not adopted, or remains pending.
tutorial.decision.amendment_vote_text: When a vote was recorded, the YES, NO, and ABSTAIN totals and the resulting decision appear here.
logs.viewer.subtitle: Research activity record
logs.viewer.limit: Latest 300 records only. Groups are ordered by their newest record; entries within each group are newest first. Filters apply only to these loaded records. Exports include all event records.
logs.viewer.timezone: Display: JST / Asia/Tokyo (UTC+09:00). Exports preserve stored timestamps without timezone conversion; an offset is present only if recorded.
logs.viewer.legend: Interaction (client): browser activity or an attempt, not proof of success. Confirmed action (semantic): an application-recorded event; inspect its action for the outcome. Request (server): an HTTP request; inspect the status. Several layers may describe one interaction—do not count them as independent participant actions. Grouping is presentation-only. Raw fields remain available below each record.
logs.viewer.no_js: Enable JavaScript to filter these records. All loaded records are shown below.
admin.event_cover_help: Optional. JPG, PNG, or WebP. Maximum 5 MB. If omitted, the default event image will be used. Images are served publicly; do not upload private material.
admin.error.event_cover_type: Choose a JPEG, PNG, or WebP image.
admin.error.event_cover_size: The cover image must be 5 MB or smaller.
admin.error.event_cover_invalid: The cover image is unreadable or unsupported. Use a still image of at most 20 megapixels.
proposal_floor.closing.archive: This floor is archived and available for review only.
proposal_floor.closing.text: Revised / Final Text Recorded at Closure
proposal_floor.closing.amendment: Revised Amendment Text Recorded at Closure
proposal_floor.closing.help: Leave blank if no revision is needed. This records the wording at the end of deliberation; the original submitted text is preserved. Recording text does not change the voting result.
proposal_floor.closing.preserved: The previously recorded closing revision will be preserved.
proposal_floor.closing.already_recorded: A closing revision is already recorded.
